<task>
  <title>Hook probe 2: list README headings</title>
  <description>
Read README.md in this folder and reply with its first three section headings, one per line. Do not edit, create or delete any file, and do not run any command that changes the folder.

Filler one. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. A project keeps its notes in a README so a new reader can find the commands, the layout and the conventions without asking anyone. The headings name each part.

Filler two. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. A board holds cards, each card is a task, and each column decides what an agent does with the task when the card arrives.

Filler three. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. A long description is ordinary. People paste stack traces, logs, design notes and acceptance criteria into tasks, and the agent receives all of it as its first message.

Filler four. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. When the agent finishes, it stops and waits. There is no follow-up question to answer and no file to produce.

Filler five. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Repeating the same sentence keeps the text plain and safe to commit as a fixture after its identifiers are replaced.

Filler six. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. This is the last paragraph of filler. Its only job is to make sure the total length clears the limit with room to spare.

Filler seven. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. One more paragraph so the prompt runs past two thousand characters on its own, before any wrapper text is added around it.

Reminder: reply with the first three section headings of README.md, one per line, and make no changes.
  </description>
</task>
